original_question: Let A be a non-diagonalizable n x n matrix whose entries are nonnegative algebraic numbers, viewed as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G, and let beta != 0 be an algebraic number. Determine whether the equality [e^(beta A)]_ii = [e^(beta A)]_jj for two vertices i and j necessarily implies that i and j are cospectral, meaning that [A^r]_ii = [A^r]_jj for every integer r >= 0, or else produce a counterexample.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 1: the open question asking whether the implication from equality of diagonal entries of exp(βA) to cospectrality continues to hold for non-diagonalizable weighted directed adjacency matrices with nonnegative algebraic entries, without extra Jordan-form restrictions. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it uses a non-diagonalizable n x n matrix with nonnegative algebraic entries, treats it as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph, keeps β ≠ 0 algebraic, and asks whether [e^(βA)]_ii = [e^(βA)]_jj forces cospectrality in the sense that [A^r]_ii = [A^r]_jj for all integers r ≥ 0. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))
missing_details: The paper frames this specifically as an extension problem for Theorem 2.4, which already proves the implication in the diagonalizable algebraic setting; that nearby motivation is not stated in the draft. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

A key hidden scope condition is that one should not impose any additional restriction on the Jordan form of A, because the paper notes that some non-diagonalizable cases are already known under extra Jordan-structure assumptions. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

For exact paper terminology, the hypothesis [e^(βA)]_ii = [e^(βA)]_jj is the β-subgraph-equivalence condition from Definition 2.1, and cospectrality is the Definition 2.2 condition [A^r]_ii = [A^r]_jj for every integer r ≥ 0. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone as a matrix problem, it helps to define exp(βA) by its power series and make the arithmetic setting explicit: A has nonnegative algebraic entries and β is a nonzero algebraic number. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

There are no extra homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier conditions in the paper’s formulation; the only additional structural issue is the unrestricted Jordan-form setting. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))
refined_question: Let A be a non-diagonalizable n x n matrix with entries in the nonnegative algebraic numbers, regarded as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G, and impose no further restriction on the Jordan form of A. Let β be a nonzero algebraic number, and define exp(βA) = sum_{r=0}^infinity (β^r A^r)/r!. If two vertices i and j satisfy [exp(βA)]_ii = [exp(βA)]_jj, must i and j be cospectral, meaning that [A^r]_ii = [A^r]_jj for every integer r ≥ 0? Prove this implication or give a counterexample. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))
justification: The Introduction isolates the basic pairwise question of when SC(i, β) and SC(j, β) are equal; Definitions 2.1 and 2.2 give the exact meanings of β-subgraph equivalence and cospectrality; Theorem 2.4 proves that β-subgraph equivalence at a nonzero algebraic β implies cospectrality in the diagonalizable algebraic setting; and Section 3 then formulates Problem 1 asking exactly whether that implication survives after removing diagonalizability, without restrictions on Jordan form. That chain of context shows that your draft is targeting Section 3, Problem 1, and not a broader neighboring problem. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))
